# Honey

<section class="hmi-quick-read" id="honey-quick-read" data-hmi-quick-read aria-labelledby="honey-quick-read-label"><div class="hmi-quick-read-label" id="honey-quick-read-label">Quick read</div>

Most monitored honey is low in metals, but lead is the one to check: the EU limit is 100 µg/kg, and small apiary surveys report much higher and less consistent results.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">European Commission · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels">Commission Regulation (EU) 2023/915 of 25 April 2023 on maximum levels for certain contaminants in food and repealing Regulation (EC) No 1881/2006</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Official Journal of the European Union</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/aghamirlou2015-iranian-honey-metals|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Aghamirlou HM, Khadem M, Rahmani A, Sadeghian M, Mahvi AH, Akbarzadeh A, Nazmara S · 2015</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/aghamirlou2015-iranian-honey-metals">Heavy metals determination in honey samples using inductively coupled plasma-optical emission spectrometry</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Journal of Environmental Health Science &amp; Engineering</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/aghamirlou2015-iranian-honey-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

<ul>
<li>
<strong>Metals of concern:</strong>

Lead decides most honey questions; cadmium, mercury and arsenic are usually near or below detection.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">U.S. Food and Drug Administration · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">FY2018-FY2020 TDS Elements Analytical Results</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">FDA Total Diet Study</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</li>
<li>
<strong>Main drivers:</strong>

Forage area and nearby industry, honey type for aluminium, and contact with metal containers.<sup class="cite">[[sources/aghamirlou2015-iranian-honey-metals|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Aghamirlou HM, Khadem M, Rahmani A, Sadeghian M, Mahvi AH, Akbarzadeh A, Nazmara S · 2015</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/aghamirlou2015-iranian-honey-metals">Heavy metals determination in honey samples using inductively coupled plasma-optical emission spectrometry</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Journal of Environmental Health Science &amp; Engineering</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/aghamirlou2015-iranian-honey-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/tomczyk2020-polish-honey-metal-transfer|5]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Tomczyk M, Zagula G, Puchalski C, Dzugan M · 2020</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/tomczyk2020-polish-honey-metal-transfer">Transfer of some toxic metals from soil to honey depending on bee habitat conditions</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Acta Universitatis Cibiniensis Series E: Food Technology</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/tomczyk2020-polish-honey-metal-transfer">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/manouchehri2021-honey-heavy-metals-review|6]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Manouchehri A, Pirhadi M, Shokri S, Khaniki GJ, Shamaei S, Miranzadeh MH · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/manouchehri2021-honey-heavy-metals-review">The Possible Effects of Heavy Metals in Honey as Toxic and Carcinogenic Substances on Human Health: A Systematic Review</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Arı Dergisi / Uludag Bee Journal</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/manouchehri2021-honey-heavy-metals-review">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</li>
<li>
<strong>Practical framing:</strong>

Ask for lot-specific lead results with a quantification limit well below 100 µg/kg.<sup class="cite">[[sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">European Commission · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels">Commission Regulation (EU) 2023/915 of 25 April 2023 on maximum levels for certain contaminants in food and repealing Regulation (EC) No 1881/2006</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Official Journal of the European Union</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">U.S. Food and Drug Administration · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">FY2018-FY2020 TDS Elements Analytical Results</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">FDA Total Diet Study</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</li>
</ul>
</section>

## Honey overview

<a id="hmi-ing-004"></a>
<a id="which-contamination-concerns-are-supported-for-this-ingredient-and-its-defined-forms"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-005"></a>

<a id="hmi-ing-006"></a>
<a id="which-evidence-gaps-most-limit-those-decisions"></a>

Large monitoring datasets find most honey lead, cadmium and mercury results at or below their reporting limits.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">U.S. Food and Drug Administration · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">FY2018-FY2020 TDS Elements Analytical Results</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">FDA Total Diet Study</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> In WHO GEMS/Food, about one third of 4,901 European lead results and about a quarter of 1,000 results from the Americas were above detection, and the most recent European period had the fewest results definitely above the EU limit.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> All three FDA Total Diet Study honey composites from 2018–2020 were below every reporting limit, including 4 µg/kg for lead.<sup class="cite">[[sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">U.S. Food and Drug Administration · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">FY2018-FY2020 TDS Elements Analytical Results</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">FDA Total Diet Study</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

Lead is still the metal that decides most honey questions. The EU sets a binding maximum of 0.10 mg/kg (100 µg/kg) for lead in honey and no honey limit for the other metals.<sup class="cite">[[sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">European Commission · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels">Commission Regulation (EU) 2023/915 of 25 April 2023 on maximum levels for certain contaminants in food and repealing Regulation (EC) No 1881/2006</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Official Journal of the European Union</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Australia’s total diet studies found lead in honey at a median of 40 µg/kg and later a mean of 24 µg/kg, placing honey among the highest-lead foods tested, though honey contributed little to most people’s lead intake.<sup class="cite">[[sources/fsanz2019-25th-australian-total-diet-study|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Food Standards Australia New Zealand · 2019</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fsanz2019-25th-australian-total-diet-study">25th Australian Total Diet Study</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Food Standards Australia New Zealand</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fsanz2019-25th-australian-total-diet-study">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/fsanz2011-23rd-australian-total-diet-study|8]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Food Standards Australia New Zealand · 2011</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fsanz2011-23rd-australian-total-diet-study">The 23rd Australian Total Diet Study</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Food Standards Australia New Zealand</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fsanz2011-23rd-australian-total-diet-study">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

Small apiary surveys tell a different and less consistent story. Means of 90–190 µg/kg in eastern Morocco and 205–935 µg/kg across four Iranian regions sit above the pooled honey reference, while Balkan and Turkish surveys and most Polish surveys sit within it.<sup <a id="ingredient-identity-and-scope"></a>
## What counts as honey

<p>Each row is one statistic a source reports for one subgroup and metal; a mean, median and range from the same samples are separate rows. Ratings place a reported mean, median or sample result against a pooled HMI reference built from every compatible honey sampling family. Same-study contrasts compare a subgroup with its own study total. Held rows failed a check against their own paper and are shown but not compared.</p>

No matched reference or pooled distribution is inferred.</p></div></details><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure" data-baseline-fallback id="hmi-reference-hmi-pooled-reference-v2:honey-pooled-Pb:371e4714b3b4"><summary>HMI honey Pb reference · 8 sampling families</summary><div data-baseline-reference-template="hmi-pooled-reference-v2:honey-pooled-Pb:371e4714b3b4"><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Reference and scope</p><p>HMI honey Pb reference · 8 sampling families. Honey as sold or collected, µg/kg; no moisture conversion. Distribution of subgroup median concentration values.</p><div class="hmi-drawer-table"><table><thead><tr><th scope="col">Reference (µg/kg)</th><th scope="col">Q1</th><th scope="col">Median</th><th scope="col">Q3</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>Primary HMI reference</td><td>≤10</td><td>40</td><td>75</td></tr><tr><td>Alternative weighting</td><td>≤10</td><td>40</td><td>75</td></tr></tbody></table></div><p>87 reference units; 8 sampling families. Counts describe evidence units, not independent studies or certainty.</p><div class="hmi-drawer-table"><table><thead><tr><th scope="col">Contributing family</th><th scope="col">Reference units</th><th scope="col">Weight</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>WHO GEMS/Food</td><td>45</td><td>13%</td></tr><tr><td>FDA TDS FY2018–FY2020</td><td>1</td><td>13%</td></tr><tr><td>Limani et al. 2021</td><td>5</td><td>13%</td></tr><tr><td>Shukla et al. 2020</td><td>14</td><td>12%</td></tr><tr><td>Aburas et al. 2023</td><td>3</td><td>13%</td></tr><tr><td>FSANZ 23rd ATDS</td><td>1</td><td>13%</td></tr><tr><td>Kazi-Tani et al. 2026</td><td>14</td><td>12%</td></tr><tr><td>Naccari et al. 2025</td><td>4</td><td>13%</td></tr></tbody></table></div><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Methods</p><p>HMI pools subgroup medians from every compatible honey sampling family in the evidence ledger: WHO GEMS/Food region-by-year medians (random sampling only), the FDA Total Diet Study composites, per-sample results printed by individual surveys, and published subgroup medians. Each family has equal total weight; subgroups have equal weight within a family. Non-detects stay as zero-to-limit intervals, so quartiles carry lower and upper bounds. Means, ranges and maxima never enter as observations.</p><p>Inverse weighted empirical CDF; midpoint at exact cumulative-weight boundaries. At least four reference units and a definitely positive Q1 to Q3 spread are required. This is a display eligibility rule, not statistical validation.</p><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Limitations</p><p>An international evidence-library reference, not a probability sample of the world honey market. GEMS/Food regions are reporting regions, not production origins. Many submissions are non-detects with differing limits, which widens the bounds. A position is descriptive concentration, not a safety or compliance judgment.</p><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Admitted source families</p><ul><li><a href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants" class="internal" data-slug="sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants" data-no-cite-meta>WHO GEMS/Food</a></li><li><a href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020" class="internal" data-slug="sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020" data-no-cite-meta>FDA TDS FY2018–FY2020</a></li><li><a href="../sources/bektashi2021-honey-metals-sugars-balkans" class="internal" data-slug="sources/bektashi2021-honey-metals-sugars-balkans" data-no-cite-meta>Limani et al. 2021</a></li><li><a href="../sources/shukla2020-honey-prayagraj-metals" class="internal" data-slug="sources/shukla2020-honey-prayagraj-metals" data-no-cite-meta>Shukla et al. 2020</a></li><li><a href="../sources/aburas2023-libyan-honey-lead-cadmium" class="internal" data-slug="sources/aburas2023-libyan-honey-lead-cadmium" data-no-cite-meta>Aburas et al. 2023</a></li><li><a href="../sources/fsanz2011-23rd-australian-total-diet-study" class="internal" data-slug="sources/fsanz2011-23rd-australian-total-diet-study" data-no-cite-meta>FSANZ 23rd ATDS</a></li><li><a href="../sources/kazitani2026-poland-algeria-honey-toxic-elements" class="internal" data-slug="sources/kazitani2026-poland-algeria-honey-toxic-elements" data-no-cite-meta>Kazi-Tani et al. 2026</a></li><li><a href="../sources/naccari2025-honey-toxic-metals-microelements" class="internal" data-slug="sources/naccari2025-honey-toxic-metals-microelements" data-no-cite-meta>Naccari et al. 2025</a></li></ul><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure"><summary>Reference version and interpretation</summary><p>Frozen evidence selection: 2026-10-22. The position remains unresolved under this alternative. This check does not address all sampling, rounding or analytical uncertainty.</p><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Sensitivity to source selection</p><ul><li>Without WHO GEMS/Food: Limited data.</li><li>Without FDA TDS FY2018–FY2020: Limited data.</li><li>Without Limani et al. 2021: Limited data.</li><li>Without Shukla et al. 2020: Limited data.</li><li>Without Aburas et al. 2023: Limited data.</li><li>Without Kazi-Tani et al. 2026: Limited data.</li><li>Without Naccari et al. 2025: Limited data.</li></ul><p>These checks show dependence on each sampling family; they are not confidence intervals.</p><div data-baseline-reference="hmi-pooled-reference-v2:honey-pooled-Cd:481813973723"><a href="#hmi-reference-hmi-pooled-reference-v2:honey-pooled-Cd:481813973723">Reference, contributing evidence and methods</a></div></div><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Collection period</p><p data-timeline-scope>2014</p><div data-selected-timeline><p>No year-by-year sample register is reconstructed from this summary.</p></div><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Geographic scope</p><p data-regional-scope>Yalova chestnut honey</p><div data-selected-regional><p>All samples in the study.</p></div><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Sampling, analysis and reporting limits</p><p>0.5 g honey + 10 mL 65% HNO3 + 1 mL 30% H2O2, microwave digestion (Berghof MWS-3+), ICP-OES (Perkin Elmer Optima 2100DV) per Methods; Results text says ICP-MS (internal inconsistency).</p><p>No LOD reported; source does not say how (or whether) non-detects occurred or were treated.</p><p>Source unit &#39;µg/kg&#39; / &#39;ppb&#39;; measurement uncertainty ±0.001 µg/kg printed per analyte. Source detection limits are given only in mg/L of measured solution (Table 2, p. 5); they are not converted to µg/kg here. <a id="sources-and-contamination-pathways"></a>
## How metals reach honey

<a id="hmi-ing-010"></a>
<a id="what-evidence-supports-root-uptake-surface-deposition-feed-transfer-or-other-biological-pathways"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-011"></a>
<a id="what-contamination-can-arise-from-agricultural-inputs-harvesting-processing-equipment-or-packaging"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-012"></a>
<a id="which-source-attribution-claims-are-measured-modelled-inferred-or-unresolved"></a>

Metals reach honey mainly through what bees collect: nectar and honeydew from plants rooted in local soil, and particles deposited from the air.<sup class="cite">[[sources/tomczyk2020-polish-honey-metal-transfer|5]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Tomczyk M, Zagula G, Puchalski C, Dzugan M · class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Acta Universitatis Cibiniensis Series E: Food Technology</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/tomczyk2020-polish-honey-metal-transfer">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/manouchehri2021-honey-heavy-metals-review|6]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Manouchehri A, Pirhadi M, Shokri S, Khaniki GJ, Shamaei S, Miranzadeh MH · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/manouchehri2021-honey-heavy-metals-review">The Possible Effects of Heavy Metals in Honey as Toxic and Carcinogenic Substances on Human Health: A Systematic Review</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Arı Dergisi / Uludag Bee Journal</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/manouchehri2021-honey-heavy-metals-review">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/margaoan2024-bee-products-heavy-metals|23]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Margaoan R, Papa G, Nicolescu A, Cornea-Cipcigan M, Kosoglu M, Topal E, Negri I · 2024</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/margaoan2024-bee-products-heavy-metals">Environmental pollution effect on honey bees and their derived products: a comprehensive analysis</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Environmental Science and Pollution Research</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/margaoan2024-bee-products-heavy-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> The best measured chain in the ledger, from Podkarpackie in Poland, found lead falling at every step from soil (21.3 mg/kg) to plants (0.52), bees (0.13) and honey (0.05 mg/kg).<sup class="cite">[[sources/tomczyk2020-polish-honey-metal-transfer|5]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Tomczyk M, Zagula G, Puchalski C, Dzugan M · 2020</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/tomczyk2020-polish-honey-metal-transfer">Transfer of some toxic metals from soil to honey depending on bee habitat conditions</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Acta Universitatis Cibiniensis Series E: Food Technology</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/tomczyk2020-polish-honey-metal-transfer">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Cadmium followed the same pattern, with honey at about a thirtieth of the level in bee bodies (0.02 against 0.63 mg/kg), and its movement along the chain was faster on acidic soils.<sup class="cite">[[sources/tomczyk2020-polish-honey-metal-transfer|5]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Tomczyk M, Zagula G, Puchalski C, Dzugan M · 2020</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/tomczyk2020-polish-honey-metal-transfer">Transfer of some toxic metals from soil to honey depending on bee habitat conditions</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Acta Universitatis Cibiniensis Series E: Food Technology</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/tomczyk2020-polish-honey-metal-transfer">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

Location effects are real but uneven. In north-west Iran, honey from the most industrialised district averaged 935 µg/kg lead against 205–595 µg/kg elsewhere, the only metal with a significant regional difference.<sup class="cite">[[sources/aghamirlou2015-iranian-honey-metals|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Aghamirlou HM, Khadem M, Rahmani A, Sadeghian M, Mahvi AH, Akbarzadeh A, Nazmara S · 2015</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/aghamirlou2015-iranian-honey-metals">Heavy metals determination in honey samples using inductively coupled plasma-optical emission spectrometry</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Journal of Environmental Health Science &amp; Engineering</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/aghamirlou2015-iranian-honey-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> In Poland, by contrast, honeys from urbanised and ecologically clean areas were comparable for cadmium, lead, aluminium and nickel.<sup class="cite">[[sources/tomczyk2020-polish-honey-metal-transfer|5]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Tomczyk M, Zagula G, Puchalski C, Dzugan M · 2020</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/tomczyk2020-polish-honey-metal-transfer">Transfer of some toxic metals from soil to honey depending on bee habitat conditions</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Acta Universitatis Cibiniensis Series E: Food Technology</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/tomczyk2020-polish-honey-metal-transfer">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> A review of bee studies also reports substantial cadmium in bees from farmland and apparently unpolluted rural areas, sometimes above industrial sites.<sup class="cite">[[sources/knoll2024-honeybee-cadmium-review|24]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Knoll S, Cappai MG · 2024</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/knoll2024-honeybee-cadmium-review">Foraging Activity of Honey Bees (Apis mellifera L., 1758) and Exposure to Cadmium: a Review</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Not reported</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/knoll2024-honeybee-cadmium-review">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

Contact after harvest is a plausible second route. Honey is acidic, and reviews and survey authors warn that bare metal, soldered or galvanised containers can add lead, tin, chromium or zinc; none of the sources measured this directly in honey.<sup class="cite">[[sources/aghamirlou2015-iranian-honey-metals|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Aghamirlou HM, Khadem M, Rahmani A, Sadeghian M, Mahvi AH, Akbarzadeh A, Nazmara S · 2015</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/aghamirlou2015-iranian-honey-metals">Heavy metals determination in honey samples using inductively coupled plasma-optical emission spectrometry</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Journal of Environmental Health Science &amp; Engineering</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/aghamirlou2015-iranian-honey-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/manouchehri2021-honey-heavy-metals-review|6]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Manouchehri A, Pirhadi M, Shokri S, Khaniki GJ, Shamaei S, Miranzadeh MH · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/manouchehri2021-honey-heavy-metals-review">The Possible Effects of Heavy Metals in Honey as Toxic and Carcinogenic Substances on Human Health: A Systematic Review</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Arı Dergisi / Uludag Bee Journal</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/manouchehri2021-honey-heavy-metals-review">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/teferi2026-honey-ethiopia-kellem-wollega|14]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Teferi AN, Dibabe YB, Debalke AG, Beyene TW, Feng W, Ho C · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/teferi2026-honey-ethiopia-kellem-wollega">Assessment of Heavy Metal Contamination and Associated Health Risks in Honey from Kellem Wollega Zone, Ethiopia</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Toxics</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/teferi2026-honey-ethiopia-kellem-wollega">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

In Calabria, chestnut honey had the lowest lead mean (79 µg/kg) and wildflower the highest (125 µg/kg), with 80% of wildflower samples above 100 µg/kg against 25% of chestnut and heather honeys.<sup class="cite">[[sources/naccari2025-honey-toxic-metals-microelements|17]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Naccari C, Ferrantelli V, Cammilleri G, Barbaccia G, Riolo P, Ferrante MC, Procopio A, Palma E · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/naccari2025-honey-toxic-metals-microelements">Study of Toxic Metals and Microelements in Honey as a Tool to Support Beekeeping Production and Consumer Safety</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Foods 2025, 14, 1986</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/naccari2025-honey-toxic-metals-microelements">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> In Iran the less industrial south was lowest (205 µg/kg mean).<sup class="cite">[[sources/aghamirlou2015-iranian-honey-metals|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Aghamirlou HM, Khadem M, Rahmani A, Sadeghian M, Mahvi AH, Akbarzadeh A, Nazmara S · 2015</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/aghamirlou2015-iranian-honey-metals">Heavy metals determination in honey samples using inductively coupled plasma-optical emission spectrometry</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Journal of Environmental Health Science &amp; Engineering</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/aghamirlou2015-iranian-honey-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> These are tentative patterns from one region each, not a supported preference for a floral type everywhere.

Cadmium, mercury and arsenic are usually low, so their comparisons rarely change a decision.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">U.S. Food and Drug Administration · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">FY2018-FY2020 TDS Elements Analytical Results</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">FDA Total Diet Study</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> The exception in the library is the same small Polish study, which reported arsenic up to 287.72 µg/kg in one organic honey in its Table 4 but a maximum of 387 µg/kg in its Table 6; both are shown as printed.<sup class="cite">[[sources/wilczynska2026-poland-organic-honey-metals|12]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Wilczyńska A, Żak N, Stasiuk E · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/wilczynska2026-poland-organic-honey-metals">Selected Toxic Elements and Pesticide Residues in Organic and Conventional Honey from Poland: A Preliminary Comparative Study</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Agriculture 2026, 16, 2154</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/wilczynska2026-poland-organic-honey-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> European GEMS/Food cadmium results above detection had a median of 7.5 µg/kg, and US composites were below 1 µg/kg.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">U.S. Food and Drug Administration · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">FY2018-FY2020 TDS Elements Analytical Results</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">FDA Total Diet Study</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Aluminium is the exception that moves with type: Polish honeydew honey carried far more aluminium than the blossom honeys from the same apiaries.<sup class="cite">[[sources/tomczyk2020-polish-honey-metal-transfer|5]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Tomczyk M, Zagula G, Puchalski C, Dzugan M · 2020</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/tomczyk2020-polish-honey-metal-transfer">Transfer of some toxic metals from soil to honey depending on bee habitat conditions</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Acta Universitatis Cibiniensis Series E: Food Technology</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/tomczyk2020-polish-honey-metal-transfer">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="which-honey-types-measured-lowest-in-lead" data-anchor="which-honey-types-measured-lowest-in-lead" data-question="Which honey types measured lowest in lead?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Which honey types measured lowest in lead?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

In the one study comparing floral types side by side, Calabrian chestnut honey averaged 79 µg/kg lead, below citrus (124), honeydew (109), heather (104) and wildflower (125 µg/kg).<sup class="cite">[[sources/naccari2025-honey-toxic-metals-microelements|17]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Naccari C, Ferrantelli V, Cammilleri G, Barbaccia G, Riolo P, Ferrante MC, Procopio A, Palma E · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/naccari2025-honey-toxic-metals-microelements">Study of Toxic Metals and Microelements in Honey as a Tool to Support Beekeeping Production and Consumer Safety</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Foods 2025, 14, 1986</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/naccari2025-honey-toxic-metals-microelements">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> In Morocco, thyme honey averaged 90 µg/kg and multifloral 190 µg/kg.<sup class="cite">[[sources/abeslami2025-moroccan-honey-minerals|10]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Abeslami A, El Farissi H, Cacciola F, El Bachiri A, Sindic M, Fauconnier ML, Bruneau E, Talhaoui A · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/abeslami2025-moroccan-honey-minerals">Unveiling the Mineral and Sugar Richness of Moroccan Honeys: A Study of Botanical Origins and Quality Indicators</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Molecules</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/abeslami2025-moroccan-honey-minerals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Each pattern comes from one region and a handful of samples per type.

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="is-urban-honey-higher-in-metals-than-rural-honey" data-anchor="is-urban-honey-higher-in-metals-than-rural-honey" data-question="Is urban honey higher in metals than rural honey?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Is urban honey higher in metals than rural honey?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Not consistently. In Poland, honeys from urbanised and ecologically clean areas were comparable for all four measured metals.<sup class="cite">[[sources/tomczyk2020-polish-honey-metal-transfer|5]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Tomczyk M, Zagula G, Puchalski C, Dzugan M · 2020</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/tomczyk2020-polish-honey-metal-transfer">Transfer of some toxic metals from soil to honey depending on bee habitat conditions</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Acta Universitatis Cibiniensis Series E: Food Technology</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/tomczyk2020-polish-honey-metal-transfer">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> In north-west Iran, the most industrialised district had the highest lead, and in Prayagraj, India, lead was detected in only four of fourteen hives, in both urban and rural sites.<sup class="cite">[[sources/aghamirlou2015-iranian-honey-metals|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Aghamirlou HM, Khadem M, Rahmani A, Sadeghian M, Mahvi AH, Akbarzadeh A, Nazmara S · 2015</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/aghamirlou2015-iranian-honey-metals">Heavy metals determination in honey samples using inductively coupled plasma-optical emission spectrometry</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Journal of Environmental Health Science &amp; Engineering</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/aghamirlou2015-iranian-honey-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/shukla2020-honey-prayagraj-metals|22]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Shukla V, Kumar A · 2020</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/shukla2020-honey-prayagraj-metals">Melissopalynological and physicochemical analysis of honey samples from Prayagraj District, Uttar Pradesh</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Acta Palaeobotanica</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/shukla2020-honey-prayagraj-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>


<a id="processing-effects"></a>
<a id="ingredient-derivative-risk"></a>
<a id="processing-effects-and-derivatives"></a>
## Processing, storage and packaging

<a id="hmi-ing-016"></a>
<a id="how-do-specified-processing-or-preparation-steps-change-the-measured-metal-endpoints"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-017"></a>
<a id="how-do-derivatives-concentrates-extracts-and-fractions-differ-from-their-parent-ingredient"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-018"></a>
<a id="do-changes-reflect-removal-redistribution-moisture-or-yield-change-dilution-or-altered-species-or-availability"></a>

No source in the ledger measured a processing step, filtration or storage time against a control for metals in honey. The processing evidence is guidance: avoid soldered, uncoated or galvanised metal containers for acidic honey, and be aware that aluminium equipment may add aluminium.<sup class="cite">[[sources/aghamirlou2015-iranian-honey-metals|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Aghamirlou HM, Khadem M, Rahmani A, Sadeghian M, Mahvi AH, Akbarzadeh A, Nazmara S · 2015</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/aghamirlou2015-iranian-honey-metals">Heavy metals determination in honey samples using inductively coupled plasma-optical emission spectrometry</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Journal of Environmental Health Science &amp; Engineering</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/aghamirlou2015-iranian-honey-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/manouchehri2021-honey-heavy-metals-review|6]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Manouchehri A, Pirhadi M, Shokri S, Khaniki GJ, Shamaei S, Miranzadeh MH · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/manouchehri2021-honey-heavy-metals-review">The Possible Effects of Heavy Metals in Honey as Toxic and Carcinogenic Substances on Human Health: A Systematic Review</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Arı Dergisi / Uludag Bee Journal</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/manouchehri2021-honey-heavy-metals-review">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/naccari2025-honey-toxic-metals-microelements|17]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Naccari C, Ferrantelli V, Cammilleri G, Barbaccia G, Riolo P, Ferrante MC, Procopio A, Palma E · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/naccari2025-honey-toxic-metals-microelements">Study of Toxic Metals and Microelements in Honey as a Tool to Support Beekeeping Production and Consumer Safety</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Foods 2025, 14, 1986</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/naccari2025-honey-toxic-metals-microelements">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> One review notes comb (waxed) honey carrying more lead than other samples and attributes it to metal storage and wax; that is an observation from cited studies, not a tested effect.<sup class="cite">[[sources/manouchehri2021-honey-heavy-metals-review|6]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Manouchehri A, Pirhadi M, Shokri S, Khaniki GJ, Shamaei S, Miranzadeh MH · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/manouchehri2021-honey-heavy-metals-review">The Possible Effects of Heavy Metals in Honey as Toxic and Carcinogenic Substances on Human Health: A Systematic Review</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Arı Dergisi / Uludag Bee Journal</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/manouchehri2021-honey-heavy-metals-review">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>



<a id="mitigation-options"></a>
## Mitigation from apiary to jar

<a id="hmi-ing-019"></a>
<a id="which-prevention-mitigation-or-remediation-measures-have-been-evaluated-for-this-ingredient"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-020"></a>
<a id="under-what-conditions-at-which-stage-and-against-which-comparator-do-they-work-or-fail"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-021"></a>
<a id="what-evidence-supports-field-or-commercial-implementation-and-ongoing-verification"></a>

Controls for honey act at the apiary, at extraction and storage, and at the release test. The only measured comparisons are observational: siting away from industrial districts coincided with lower lead in Iran, while urban and clean habitats did not differ in Poland.<sup class="cite">[[sources/aghamirlou2015-iranian-honey-metals|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Aghamirlou HM, Khadem M, Rahmani A, Sadeghian M, Mahvi AH, Akbarzadeh A, Nazmara S · 2015</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/aghamirlou2015-iranian-honey-metals">Heavy metals determination in honey samples using inductively coupled plasma-optical emission spectrometry</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Journal of Environmental Health Science &amp; Engineering</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/aghamirlou2015-iranian-honey-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/tomczyk2020-polish-honey-metal-transfer|5]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Tomczyk M, Zagula G, Puchalski C, Dzugan M · 2020</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/tomczyk2020-polish-honey-metal-transfer">Transfer of some toxic metals from soil to honey depending on bee habitat conditions</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Acta Universitatis Cibiniensis Series E: Food Technology</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/tomczyk2020-polish-honey-metal-transfer">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Container and equipment controls are guidance without measured effects, and testing detects lead without removing it.<sup class="cite">[[sources/aghamirlou2015-iranian-honey-metals|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Aghamirlou HM, Khadem M, Rahmani A, Sadeghian M, Mahvi AH, Akbarzadeh A, Nazmara S · 2015</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/aghamirlou2015-iranian-honey-metals">Heavy metals determination in honey samples using inductively coupled plasma-optical emission spectrometry</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Journal of Environmental Health Science &amp; Engineering</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/aghamirlou2015-iranian-honey-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/manouchehri2021-honey-heavy-metals-review|6]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Manouchehri A, Pirhadi M, Shokri S, Khaniki GJ, Shamaei S, Miranzadeh MH · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/manouchehri2021-honey-heavy-metals-review">The Possible Effects of Heavy Metals in Honey as Toxic and Carcinogenic Substances on Human Health: A Systematic Review</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Arı Dergisi / Uludag Bee Journal</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/manouchehri2021-honey-heavy-metals-review">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/zhang2024-mip-pb-honey-cyprus|16]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Karagozlu M, Asir S, Abu Shama N, Gokturk I, Yilmaz F, Turkmen D, Denizli A, Ozgoren M · 2024</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/zhang2024-mip-pb-honey-cyprus">Development of Molecularly Imprinted Magnetic Amino Acid-Based Nanoparticles for Voltammetric Analysis of Lead Ions in Honey</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Polymers 2024, 16, 1782</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/zhang2024-mip-pb-honey-cyprus">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="why-do-some-studies-report-very-high-lead-in-honey" data-anchor="why-do-some-studies-report-very-high-lead-in-honey" data-question="Why do some studies report very high lead in honey?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Why do some studies report very high lead in honey?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Some very high values do not survive a check against their own papers. One Ethiopian study reports about 20 mg/kg lead, a level its own detection limits could not have measured after its stated dilution, and a Libyan survey reports 2.4–11 mg/kg means with no quality control.<sup class="cite">[[sources/teferi2026-honey-ethiopia-kellem-wollega|14]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Teferi AN, Dibabe YB, Debalke AG, Beyene TW, Feng W, Ho C · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/teferi2026-honey-ethiopia-kellem-wollega">Assessment of Heavy Metal Contamination and Associated Health Risks in Honey from Kellem Wollega Zone, Ethiopia</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Toxics</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/teferi2026-honey-ethiopia-kellem-wollega">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/salama2019-libya-honey-metals|15]]<span class="cite-card"><span single values without replicate or method detail.<sup class="cite">[[sources/aburas2023-libyan-honey-lead-cadmium|18]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span Honey is eaten in small amounts, so even its relatively high lead median adds little to most diets.<sup class="cite">[[sources/fsanz2019-25th-australian-total-diet-study|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Food Standards Australia New Zealand · 2019</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fsanz2019-25th-australian-total-diet-study">25th Australian Total Diet Study</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Food Standards Australia New Zealand</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fsanz2019-25th-australian-total-diet-study">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Australia’s 25th Total Diet Study found honey was a minor contributor to lead exposure for every age group except children aged 2–5, where it contributed 6%.<sup class="cite">[[sources/fsanz2019-25th-australian-total-diet-study|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Food Standards Australia New Zealand · 2019</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fsanz2019-25th-australian-total-diet-study">25th Australian Total Diet Study</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Food Standards Australia New Zealand</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fsanz2019-25th-australian-total-diet-study">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

One US paper reports that honey intakes exceed tolerable weekly limits, but its intake table is mislabelled by a factor of 1,000.<sup class="cite">[[sources/wise2025-elevated-metals-us-honeys|13]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Wise JP Jr, Wise RM, Hoffert A, Wise JTF, Specht AJ · <a id="universal-faqs"></a>
## Honey FAQs

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="what-heavy-metals-are-found-in-honey" data-anchor="what-heavy-metals-are-found-in-honey" data-question="What heavy metals are found in honey?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>What heavy metals are found in honey?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Lead is the metal most often found at levels that matter; cadmium, mercury and arsenic are usually low or below detection.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">U.S. Food and Drug Administration · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">FY2018-FY2020 TDS Elements Analytical Results</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">FDA Total Diet Study</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Honey can also contain aluminium, nickel and chromium, which vary with honey type and processing.<sup class="cite">[[sources/tomczyk2020-polish-honey-metal-transfer|5]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Tomczyk M, Zagula G, Puchalski C, Dzugan M · 2020</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/tomczyk2020-polish-honey-metal-transfer">Transfer of some toxic metals from soil to honey depending on bee habitat conditions</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Acta Universitatis Cibiniensis Series E: Food Technology</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/tomczyk2020-polish-honey-metal-transfer">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/naccari2025-honey-toxic-metals-microelements|17]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Naccari C, Ferrantelli V, Cammilleri G, Barbaccia G, Riolo P, Ferrante MC, Procopio A, Palma E · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/naccari2025-honey-toxic-metals-microelements">Study of Toxic Metals and Microelements in class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Limani Bektashi N, Abazi D, Popovska O, Latifi A, Reka AA · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" <details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="how-do-heavy-metals-get-into-honey" data-anchor="how-do-heavy-metals-get-into-honey" data-question="How do heavy metals get into honey?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>How do heavy metals get into honey?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Bees carry metals from nectar, honeydew and airborne dust into the hive, but much is filtered out along the way.<sup class="cite">[[sources/tomczyk2020-polish-honey-metal-transfer|5]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Tomczyk M, Zagula G, Puchalski C, Dzugan M · 2020</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/tomczyk2020-polish-honey-metal-transfer">Transfer of some toxic metals from soil to honey depending on bee habitat conditions</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Acta Universitatis Cibiniensis Series E: Food Technology</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/tomczyk2020-polish-honey-metal-transfer">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/manouchehri2021-honey-heavy-metals-review|6]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Manouchehri A, Pirhadi M, Shokri S, Khaniki GJ, Shamaei S, Miranzadeh MH · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/manouchehri2021-honey-heavy-metals-review">The Possible Effects of Heavy Metals in Honey as Toxic and Carcinogenic Substances on Human Health: A Systematic Review</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Arı Dergisi / Uludag Bee Journal</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/manouchehri2021-honey-heavy-metals-review">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> In Poland, lead fell from 21.3 mg/kg in soil to 0.05 mg/kg in honey.<sup class="cite">[[sources/tomczyk2020-polish-honey-metal-transfer|5]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Tomczyk M, Zagula G, Puchalski C, Dzugan M · 2020</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/tomczyk2020-polish-honey-metal-transfer">Transfer of some toxic metals from soil to honey depending on bee habitat conditions</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Acta Universitatis Cibiniensis Series E: Food Technology</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/tomczyk2020-polish-honey-metal-transfer">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>
